full_instruction: Find flights from Boston to Tokyo next month, business class, using points if available.
Find a hotel near Shinjuku Station for three nights, but not a capsule hotel.
Plan a rental car at JFK for Friday, then actually switch it to Newark because my arrival airport changed.
Find a nonstop flight to Chicago, unless nonstop is over $200 more, then allow one stop.
Find an Italian restaurant near my hotel for dinner, but I need one with outdoor seating.
Find a coffee shop open early tomorrow; actually I need a bakery that also serves coffee.
Find a gym nearby with a day pass, preferably one with a sauna.
Find a pharmacy open now, but exclude stores inside hospitals.
Research U.S. manufacturers of robotic actuators that could substitute for Chinese suppliers, and identify distributors specializing in U.S.-made parts.
Compare two 15L cross-body bags with handles, but prioritize weight over laptop padding.
Find a brown faux-suede men's jacket with a stand collar under $200.
Research synthetic data tools for robotics, especially Unreal Engine, but exclude purely visual rendering tools with no physics support.
Find a compact standing desk converter under $250, but not one that requires permanent mounting.
Schedule a 30-minute meeting with Alex next week, preferably Tuesday afternoon.
Move my dentist appointment to Friday; if Friday is unavailable, keep the current appointment.
Find time for a team sync this week, but not before 10 AM.
Remind me to submit the report tomorrow evening, not in the morning.
Draft an email to the recruiter thanking them and saying I'm happy to provide anything else useful for the evaluation.
Write a Slack message saying the build is delayed, but don't blame the infrastructure team.
Draft a polite text declining dinner tonight and suggest next weekend instead.
Write a customer reply confirming the refund was approved, but do not promise the posting date.
Find papers on frozen-model hidden states for predicting future intent, prioritizing peer-reviewed work.
Look up the latest documentation for a Python library, but only use the official docs.
Find the current CEO and recent earnings for the company, but exclude analyst estimates.
Research regulations for consumer AI in California, not federal rules unless needed for context.
Find current benchmark results for small open-weight reasoning models, but exclude vendor self-reported numbers unless independently reproduced.
Compare QQQ and DIA downside scenarios for a 7% market decline, without recommending a trade.
Summarize my budget categories and identify the biggest variance, but don't move any money.
Check whether my portfolio concentration increased this month, using holdings only and not transaction history.
Calculate the breakeven for an options spread from the prices I provide, but do not fetch live quotes.
Write a Python function to parse the log file and return error counts, but don't modify the source file.
Debug why the API client times out, but don't change retry settings until we identify the cause.
Refactor this function for readability while preserving behavior and public API.
Create tests for the parser, focusing on malformed inputs rather than performance benchmarks.
Rewrite the memo to be shorter and more executive, but keep all numerical claims unchanged.
Summarize this report into one page, excluding the appendix.
Turn these notes into a proposal, but leave pricing as TBD.
Compare the two resume versions and identify differences, without rewriting either one.
Turn on the living-room lights at 30%, but don't change the color.
Set the thermostat to 70 tonight, unless the house is already below 68.
Lock the back door after I leave, but only if the door sensor shows it is closed.
Start the robot vacuum in the kitchen, not the whole floor.
Find a documentary about robotics, preferably under 90 minutes.
Make a playlist of upbeat jazz for work, but no vocals.
Recommend a movie for tonight, not horror and under two hours.
Find a podcast episode on AI agents, but prioritize technical interviews over news recaps.
Make a packing checklist for a three-day business trip, but don't include formalwear.
Plan my morning around a 9 AM appointment, with 30 minutes for travel.
Create a grocery list for tacos, but make it vegetarian.
Prioritize my task list for today, but keep the client deadline first even if another task is shorter.
